If you're building AI-powered features, you're probably sending a lot of JSON to language models. And if you're sending a lot of JSON, you're probably burning through tokens faster than you'd like.
At Kollabe, we use AI to generate summaries, action items, and suggestions for retrospectives and standups. When you have dozens of team members submitting updates daily, the JSON payloads get large quickly. We needed ways to shrink our data without losing information.
There are newer formal solutions out there like TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation) that can compress JSON for LLMs by up to 40%. It's a proper spec with benchmarks and SDKs. Worth checking out if you want a standardized approach.
But sometimes you want to stay in control. You don't want another dependency. You want to understan…

articles.description:
GitHub repo : https://github.com/devopsexpertlearning/docker-nginx-react-kubernetes-fullstack
Starting my first post here to share a bit about my journey in DevOps and cloud engineering.
Why I chose Containers and AWS
AWS became my preferred cloud platform because it allows you to combine managed services with full control when needed. Services like EKS, CloudFront, IAM, and CloudWatch helped me understand how production systems are actually designed and operated.
What I’m currently building
Containerized full-stack applications using Docker and Kubernetes
CI/CD pipelines to automate build and deployment workflows
Secure and scalable AWS architectures for real-world use cases
Most of my learning comes from hands-on projects, not just tutorials. Building end-to-end systems has taught me far more than isolated examples.
Why I’m sharing here
Practical Kubernetes and Docker use cases
AWS architecture patterns
DevOps automation lessons from real projects
Common mistakes and how to avoid them
My goal is to keep things simple, practical, and honest—especially for engineers who are still learning or transitioning into DevOps.
What’s next
Upcoming posts will cover:
Deploying applications on Kubernetes step by step
CI/CD best practices for containerized workloads
AWS cost, security, and observability basics
If you’re learning DevOps, cloud, or containers, feel free to say hi or share your journey too. Looking forward to learning together 🚀
